message.content:
In the Go repo at /bench/home/work (memos project), answer two aggregation questions. Be quantitative.

Q1: Among functions/methods declared under internal/ (packages internal/util, internal/base, internal/profile etc.), which single function has the highest inbound-call count (fan-in) from the rest of the codebase (Go code in server/, store/, cmd/, internal/)? Candidates to check: util.ConvertStringToInt32, base error helpers, profile methods, util.GenUUID, util.ValidateEmail, internal/base UID functions, etc. Grep for call sites of each candidate (e.g. grep -rn 'util\.' --include='*.go' | count by function). Report the winner: symbol — declaration path:line — approximate number of callers (count distinct call sites in non-test code, but mention if tests included changes ranking). Also report the runner-up.

Q2: The data layer is the store package (store/*.go) defining persistent entity structs (Memo, User, Attachment/Resource, Activity, IdentityProvider, Webhook, Reaction, MemoRelation, UserSetting, WorkspaceSetting, etc.). Which entity type is referenced from the largest number of DISTINCT Go packages outside the store package tree (i.e. server/..., internal/..., cmd/...)? Count distinct packages (directories) mentioning store.Memo vs store.User vs others (grep -rln 'store\.User\b' etc., group by directory). Report the top two with rough package counts.

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
## Q1 — Highest fan-in function declared under `internal/`

**Winner: `util.GenUUID`**
- Declaration: `/bench/home/work/internal/util/util.go:40`
- **7 distinct non-test call sites** (all cross-package), **28 total call sites including tests**

Non-test call sites:
- `/bench/home/work/server/auth/token.go:194`
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_access_tokens.go:84`
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service_storage.go:209`
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sso_username.go:15`
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go:154`
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_session.go:26` and `:135`

Test callers add 21 more, heavily concentrated in `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/test/auth_test.go` (19 calls), plus `authz_test.go` (1) and `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go` (1).

**Runner-up: `filter.DefaultEngine`**
- Declaration: `/bench/home/work/internal/filter/engine.go:111`
- **7 non-test call sites, 7 total** (no test callers) — it actually *ties* GenUUID on non-test count and only loses once tests are included. Callers: the three DB dialects (`store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/memo.go` and `.../memo_relation.go`) plus `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go:341`.

Does including tests change the ranking? Yes, materially. On non-test code alone it is a 7–7 tie between `util.GenUUID` and `filter.DefaultEngine`; adding tests makes `GenUUID` a clear winner (28 vs 7), almost entirely due to one auth test file.

Full ranked table (cross-package, non-test / total):

| Symbol | Decl | non-test | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| `util.GenUUID` | internal/util/util.go:40 | 7 | 28 |
| `filter.DefaultEngine` | internal/filter/engine.go:111 | 7 | 7 |
| `filter.AppendConditions` | internal/filter/helpers.go:9 | 6 | 6 |
| `(*filter.Engine).CompileToStatement` | internal/filter/engine.go:74 | 6 cross-pkg (7 w/ in-pkg helper) | 6 cross-pkg (38 incl. filter's own package tests) |
| `s3.NewClient` | internal/storage/s3/s3.go:25 | 5 | 5 |
| `util.ConvertStringToInt32` | internal/util/util.go:14 | 5 | 5 |
| `version.GetCurrentVersion` | internal/version/version.go:16 | 4 | 5 |
| `(*profile.Profile).AllowAnonymous` | internal/profile/profile.go:46 | 4 | 5 |

Caveats worth flagging:
- `CompileToStatement` has 38 raw grep hits but 31 are inside `internal/filter`'s own test files, so it is not the true cross-package leader.
- The other `internal/util` helpers the prompt asked about are effectively dead from a fan-in perspective: `util.ValidateEmail`, `util.HasPrefixes`, and `util.ReplaceString` have **0** call sites anywhere in `server/`, `store/`, `cmd/`, `internal/` (only their own unit tests in `/bench/home/work/internal/util/util_test.go`).
- `internal/base` declares no functions at all — it exposes a single package-level var `UIDMatcher` at `/bench/home/work/internal/base/resource_name.go:6`, used at 7 non-test sites (`store/memo.go:110,134`, `store/attachment.go:90,126`, `store/deployment_config.go:162`, `server/router/api/v1/user_resource_name.go:30`, `server/router/api/v1/resource_name.go:145`). If vars counted, it would tie for first on non-test usage.

## Q2 — Store entity referenced from the most distinct outside packages

**Winner: `store.User`** — 7 distinct packages outside the store tree (6 excluding test-only packages), 30 files, 93 references.

Packages (files each):
- `server/router/api/v1` (19)
- `server/router/api/v1/test` (3)
- `server/router/rss` (2)
- `server/router/fileserver` (2)
- `server/auth` (2)
- `server/router/frontend` (1)
- `server/notification` (1)

**Runner-up: `store.Memo`** — 6 distinct packages (4 non-test), 21 files, 64 references: `server/router/api/v1` (13), `server/router/api/v1/test` (3), `server/router/rss` (2), `server/runner/memopayload` (1), `server/router/frontend` (1), `server/notification` (1).

Third is `store.Attachment` at 4 packages (3 non-test) / 12 files / 43 refs: `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/rss`, `server/router/fileserver`. Note the entity is named `Attachment` (`/bench/home/work/store/attachment.go:16`) — there is no `store.Resource` type; that rename is complete.

The long tail drops off fast: `store.MemoRelation`, `store.Inbox`, `store.MemoShare` at 3 packages each; `store.Reaction` and `store.UserIdentity` at 2. Notably `store.Activity`, `store.Webhook`, `store.IdentityProvider`, `store.UserSetting`, `store.WorkspaceSetting`, `store.InstanceSetting`, and `store.AuthConfig` have **zero** references outside the store tree — they are either store-internal or surfaced only through generated protobuf types rather than the store struct.

One caveat on methodology: no distinct package outside the store tree reaches `store.User`'s breadth, and the gap between User and Memo is driven mostly by `server/auth` and `server/router/fileserver`, which touch users (authn/ownership) but not memos directly.
